issue.title: Epic: initial enhancements, wave 2
issue.body:
This epic collects the next wave of quiet-choir work (trimmed recording: only the items kept in this fixture).

**The checklist below is the execution order.** Each run takes the first ready item, skipping items with a "Depends on #N" line whose dependency is still open.

## Items

### 1. A faster, quieter feedback loop

- [x] #121 runner.ts: replace effect()'s 15 positional parameters with an EffectSpec and extract pure classifyAttemptFailure and decideReplay with table tests
- [x] #184 Replace effect()'s positional parameters with an EffectSpec object
- [x] #185 Extract classifyAttemptFailure into a pure attempt-failure module with ADR 0007 table tests
- [x] #186 Extract decideReplay into a pure replay-decision module with table tests

### 2. Trust: bugs that lose work, lie, or break resume

- [x] #131 Pin step-identity schema encodings with golden tests so zod bumps fail CI, and record toolchain versions

### 4. The authoring and recovery loop

- [x] #109 Enforce expectsToolUse and add idleTimeoutMs using streamed attempt events
- [x] #156 Record and show the subscription rate-limit windows Claude reports
- [x] #158 One spelling per concept at 0.0.0: remove positional map overloads, split map settle/abort, and unify worktree isolation and Codex effort
- [x] #339 Remove positional ctx.map overloads and split map onError into a result mode and cancelSiblings
- [x] #340 Make worktree the only checkout selector and narrow isolation to the harness mode
- [x] #341 Give Codex one effort option and rename reasoningEffort in policy overrides and attempt records

### 5. Built-in GitHub (advances #21)

- [x] #159 quiet-choir/github slice A: typed, complete-or-throw reads over the installed gh
- [ ] #163 quiet-choir/github slice D: epic snapshot and a pure next-ticket selector

### 6. Docs and housekeeping

- [ ] #164 Agent-facing docs: native-Workflow porting reference, a present-tense decision table, and tested CI-gate and ticket-loop recipes

### 7. Second slices, lower priority

- [ ] #167 Add a run-record schemaRevision so older builds refuse to rewrite records with fields they do not know
- [ ] #168 Add a sticky --max-window-utilization gate that suspends until the rate-limit window resets

nodes.title: runner.ts: replace effect()'s 15 positional parameters with an EffectSpec and extract pure classifyAttemptFailure and decideReplay with table tests
nodes.body:
## Summary

`effect()` in `src/workflow/runtime/runner.ts` takes 15 positional parameters, and its eight call sites pass runs of placeholders such as `null, identity, undefined, undefined, null, phase, ...`, so a swapped argument of a matching type would typecheck. Its replay decision and failure classification…
- Failure classification is in the attempt `catch` at `:1600-1712`: `scoped` (`:1616`), `infrastructure` (`:1671`), `fatal` (`:1676`), `retry` (`:1677`), then the settle-or-throw branch for `onError: 'return'`. It depends on checkpoint problems, the scope signal, `ConfigurationError`, attempt limits and `retry.on`. ADR 0007 (`docs/decisions/0007-durable-failure-outcomes.md`) specifies these outcomes in prose (cancellation, configuration failures, checkpoint failures, retry filters, settled returns) with no table.
   - `classifyAttemptFailure({ cause, scopeSignal, checkpointProblems, policy, attempt, maxAttempts, onError })` returns `{ status, retry, settle, fatal, errorKind }` for the facts known at `:1616-1682`. The post-save `signal.reason instanceof CheckpointError` check at the retry branch stays in the runner because it depends on state after `trySave()`.

Splitting this into three PRs, in order, to match the two-PR plan in the ticket. The pure-decision half is itself two independent reviews of different risk.

<!-- epic:split 184,185,186 -->

nodes.title: Pin step-identity schema encodings with golden tests so zod bumps fail CI, and record toolchain versions
nodes.body:
## Summary

Step and agent identities hash the raw output of `z.toJSONSchema`, and the CI golden-identity test feeds a literal schema, so a zod release that changes that encoding strands every suspended run without failing CI. zod is a production dependency covered by grouped weekly Dependabot minor bumps. This…
- **PR-B, stable built-in identities.** `ctx.now` (`runner.ts:2715-2720`) and `decision.choose` (`src/integrations/decision.ts:68-77`) hash their own callback text through `Function.prototype.toString` (`runner.ts:1240`), so a refactor of quiet-choir strands runs that completed them (review repro R9: rewriting `run: () => clockNow(clock)` as a block body made resume fail with "callback changed on a completed step"). The fix gives built-ins an explicit versioned identity and hashes no callback text, and needs an internal path because `decision` uses public `ctx.step`, whose `version` plus callback identity is documented (`durability.md:166-170`). An identity that embeds `schemaJson` output stays exposed to the drift above. Golden digests for these two identities belong in that PR, since callback text depends on the loader (`durability.md:166`).

nodes.title: quiet-choir/github slice D: epic snapshot and a pure next-ticket selector
nodes.body:
## Summary

The "execute the next ticket of an epic" workflow needs a complete, replay-stable view of an epic and a deterministic, explainable pick. Add `gh.epic.snapshot(id, n)`, one GraphQL `ctx.exec.json` returning the epic's sub-issues with state, labels, assignees, open blockers and linked PRs, and an expo…
4. Export `nextTicket(snapshot, policy)` as a pure function with no context argument. Candidates are open, not blocked by an open issue, and without an open linked PR. `policy` selects order: listing order or issue number. Every open item that is not picked appears in `skipped` with a reason such as `blocked` or `has-open-pr`. No pick with nothing skipped means every ticket is closed (done).
- [ ] `nextTicket` unit tests over a recorded #99-shaped snapshot cover: blocked by an open issue, has an open linked PR, all closed (done, empty `skipped`), and empty-but-incomplete (throws).
Depends on #159.
